habitat: Pairs in bushveld, woodland, riverine forest and suburbia, including flowering creepers. Noisy and conspicuous.
summary: A common resident. The male has a large red breast-patch. The colour key says the red breast shows when the bird is perched, with iridescent green on the forehead. The female has heavy dark markings on the underparts. Newman says it replaces Amethyst Sunbird in northerly, low-lying places, with a wide overlap. The call is a high-pitched chatter and a repeated cheep, chip, chop. That description is printed on the Southern Double-collared page. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

head.pattern: Iridescent green on the forehead. Large red breast-patch. Red is the token used for the breast; the text says red, not a narrower band.

underparts.pattern: Large red breast-patch, visible when perched.
Heavy dark markings on the underparts. Separate colours were not named.

calls.description: A high-pitched chattering sound, and a much-repeated cheep, chip, chop from a prominent perch. This text is on the Southern Double-collared page. Grade A call from near Skukuza. The filename is XC1149407-20260519_KNP_AKaramitsos_XA60_A027C049_260519NT_SLE_2000HP_-3dB_SCS.mp3 and includes -3dB.

research.note: The colour key and the 15 cm size are on the Scarlet-chested page. The plumage and voice used here are printed on the Southern Double-collared page and match the red breast, which is why this needs review. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.

size.note: Newman's Birds gives 15 cm on the Scarlet-chested Sunbird page.

similar.note: Amethyst Sunbird lacks the large red breast. Scarlet-chested replaces it in northerly, low-lying places, and the ranges overlap widely.
Marico Sunbird has a claret or maroon breast-band, not a large bright red breast, and a black belly.
